summary: Both referred rulings re-verified as still present, then decided and carried out. RULING 1 (fabric): the fixer's blocking premise -- 'q_entry and halt_b have no specified shape anywhere in the reachable tree' -- is FALSE. All four names are minted with exact constructors in the frozen old tree at self_organize.py:1733 and :1907-1908. Re-reading the call sites splits the four cleanly: norm, nov_proj and halt_b are read on the walk THIS tree ports, so they are now built by FAB.build; q_entry's only three readers all belong to arms this rebuild has explicitly dropped, so it is dropped from state_dict's list exactly as ctrl was, with the reason recorded. state_dict's list and build's allocation now agree name for name. RULING 2 (ckpt): the Gate save_period's DID IT FIRE line has always claimed is now built and rides on the returned units.Windows as .gates -- the same convention FAB, CAP, MEM and TOK already use -- because a shape change or a new entry point both land in files this package does not own, measured rather than assumed. recommendation.chose: RULING 1: build norm, nov_proj and halt_b in FAB.build to the frozen old tree's own constructors; drop q_entry from FAB.state_dict's parameter list with the reason recorded, reversing this docstring's own earlier 'both walks use them' ruling; allocate halt_key with bias=False so the learned halt prior exists once, under the name the contract gives it. RULING 2: save_period keeps returning a bare units.Windows (unchanged type, unchanged call shape) and attaches Gate('ckpt.periodic_armed', ...) to it as a .gates tuple, with all three of spine/gate.py's states spelled out; the package-wide gates() accessor is reported as a referred edit rather than taken unilaterally.
recommendation.alternatives: RULING 1, four options weighed. (a) Build all four. REJECTED for q_entry once its readers were traced: all three sit on arms this rebuild dropped, so building it would mint a parameter with no reader and no future reader -- manufacturing the armed-but-inert shape this audit exists to remove. (b) Trim the whole list the way ctrl was trimmed. REJECTED for norm/nov_proj/halt_b: each is read on the ported soc walk, and dropping them would make a checkpoint round-trip silently lose a tensor the forward pass will need -- the 'quiet narrowing' the brief forbids. (c) Raise spine/gate.py::NotBuilt at the point of use. REJECTED on the type's own contract: NotBuilt is for an arm the owner has ruled DECLARED-AND-UNPORTED (Q-FAB-1's transition walk). None of these four is such an arm; they are unwritten allocations, and spending NotBuilt on them would collapse exactly the distinction gate.py's NotBuilt docstring exists to keep. (d) Wait for the commit that writes forward(). REJECTED because the geometry is not a guess: three constructors are literal in the frozen tree, and A, B and the other five modules are equally unexercised today for the same reason -- 'forward is a stub' argues for allocating at the recorded geometry, not for leaving a save-side claim outstanding. A FIFTH question surfaced that the referral did not name: halt_key was already nn.Linear(d_model, 1), whose own bias occupies precisely halt_b's additive position, so allocating halt_b beside it would have put two learned scalars in one place with one necessarily dead. Options were (i) accept the redundancy (rejected: manufactures the defect class), (ii) drop halt_b and rule it folded into halt_key.bias (rejected: the contract's list would lose a name a reader can grep for), (iii) halt_key bias=False and halt_b carries the prior -- chosen, because it is a 1:1 match with the old tree's decomposition (a bare key at :1724 plus a separate prior at :1733) and the parameter count is unchanged. RULING 2, four options priced by running them. (a) Return (Windows, Gate) or a small record. REJECTED: the value is read UNWRAPPED into the periods mapping at two sites in spine/compose.py (lines 2063 and 2651, a file I do not own), and both train/api.py::Cadences.due and spine/derive.py::cadences_that_cannot_fire refuse anything whose type is not exactly Windows -- a SUBCLASS raises too, verified. (b) A new public gates()/periodic_gate() accessor, which is the shape FAB/CAP/MEM/TOK effectively have. REJECTED AS A BODY FIX with the cost measured, not guessed: I added a dummy public function to ckpt/api.py and ran the suite -- K1, K6 and K13 all fail, and every repair lands in docs/04_CONTRACT.md or spine/compose.py. Reported as a referred edit. (c) Attach the Gate to the returned Windows -- CHOSEN. Zero foreign files, type unchanged, and it is the same '.gates on the object the entry point returns' convention as the four existing producers. Its one cost is stated in the docstring rather than left to be discovered: a Clock is a value object, so arithmetic or a re-wrap drops the tuple; nothing in the tree does either today. (d) Delete the Gate claim from the DID IT FIRE line. REJECTED: the condition would then be printed nowhere.
recommendation.evidence: RULING 1. self_organize.py:1907-1908 mints all of q_entry, nov and ctrl on ONE line inside __init__ -- `s.q_entry = nn.Linear(sig_d, dk); s.nov = nn.Linear(1, dk); s.ctrl = nn.Linear(3, dk)` then `s.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d)` -- and :1733 mints `s.halt_b = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1))` with the comment 'prior on halting, learned; 0 = whatever the query says'. So every one of the four has an exact shape and an exact initialisation in the frozen tree, which is what the referral said did not exist. Readers, by grep: norm at :2575 (the norm_only ablation `for _ in range(steps): h = s.norm(h)`), :2677 and :2683 (inside `if s.loop_soc:` -- the ported walk's per-hop vote and residual step), :2781 and :2814 (transition arm). nov at :2361 inside entry_logits (the grounded router this contract ports, and the very line FAB.forward cites for the M28 novelty defect), :2320, :2580. halt_b at :2442, :2596, :2628 (inside `if s.loop_soc:`) and :2841. q_entry has exactly three readers and this tree ports none of the arms behind them: :2591 the `else` of `if s.grounded:` (the ROUTE_GROUNDED=0 entry router, which the old tree's own comment at :2581-2583 calls 'a different and strictly weaker router', and which fabric/levers.py::FABLevers.cent_ema records as dropped -- 'now that ROUTE_GROUNDED's alternative router is dropped'); :2597 the `else` of `if s.halt_on` on that same branch; and :2564 seed_key, whose single caller is `s.K[j] = s.seed_key(gist)` at :2143, a write into the FREE identity parameters that fabric/levers.py::FABLevers.dk's section header records as dropped ('FAB_DERIVE_IDS=0 (free identity parameters) is dropped'). The old tree measured the consequence itself: its ROUTER LEARNING audit printed 'never gradiented -> ctrl, q_entry' at the shipped ROUTE_GROUNDED=1 (:9141, audit loop at :7085), and two armed-but-inert records in .rework/ISSUES.md (lines 1594-1595 and 1789-1790) name the SPECIALIZATION section as having partitioned the population with a randomly-initialised q_entry for the life of the probe. Two of the earlier ruling's three citations (:2554, :2557) no longer resolve to anything about either name; :2564 resolves to seed_key. FAB.forward is confirmed still a stub (`raise NotImplementedError`), which is why none of this fires at runtime today and why the mismatch was latent rather than loud. RULING 2. CKPT_DIR defaults to "" and CKPT_EVERY defaults to 0 (src/ckpt/levers.py::CKPTLevers.dir and .every, read out of the resolved Config, printed below). save_period's body was `return U.Windows(int(ckpt.every))`; spine.gate was not imported anywhere in the file. spine/compose.py names save_period's return at line 2063 (`periods = {... 'ckpt': ckpt_api.save_period(ckpt)}`) and again at 2651 inside _periods, both unwrapped -- so the shape is load-bearing outside this package. tests/test_contract.py's K9 only requires the mapping value to be a CALL, so attaching to the returned object is invisible to it, while K13's entry-point population (`_k13_entry_points`: public module-level functions and public methods in src/*/api.py) counts a new accessor immediately.
recommendation.measurement: RULING 2's decisive measurement, run through spine.assemble.build on the resolved Configs with the run length held at sixty thousand windows, BEFORE the fix. Columns: CKPT_DIR, CKPT_EVERY, saving_on(), derive.cadences_that_cannot_fire(). ""(shipped)/0 -> False / [('ckpt', 0, 0)]. runs/x/0 -> True / [('ckpt', 0, 0)]. ""(shipped)/4000 -> False / []. runs/x/4000 -> True / []. Two PAIRS of genuinely different runs rendered identically by the only artifact that mentions this cadence -- because cadences_that_cannot_fire never reads `dir`. At the shipped defaults the honest state is UNREACHABLE, not armed-but-zero: an operator who reads 'the ckpt gate cannot fire' and raises CKPT_EVERY still saves nothing. AFTER the fix, the same four configurations print, from period.gates[0].line(): UNREACHABLE (0 vs 1) / armed, did not fire (0 vs 1) with 'the only saves this run makes are the FINAL one and any SIGUSR1' / UNREACHABLE (4000 vs 1) / FIRED (4000 vs 1) -- four distinguishable readings, and type(period) is still exactly units.Windows so derive accepts it. The measurement that would settle the placement question if the evidence had not: add the accessor and run the suite. I did: K1, K6 and K13 all fail, naming docs/04_CONTRACT.md's entry-point total in seven present-tense claims across six locations and requiring a row in spine/compose.py's ASSEMBLY_ORDER/LOOP_ORDER or DEFERRED_ENTRY_POINTS. Reverted immediately (verified byte-identical against a saved copy). RULING 1's settling measurement, had the old-tree constructors not existed, would have been to write the geometry only where a live call site pins it; it was not needed, because the constructors are literal and the reader sites are greppable.
